sides.text: A router has routes to 10.1.0.0/16, 10.1.1.0/24, and 10.0.0.0/8. Which route is used for 10.1.1.55?
options: The route with the lowest metric

more.text: Longest prefix match decides first.

sides.text: Which route is preferred for the same prefix?
options: The route with the highest metric
The route with the lowest administrative distance
The route with the longest AD

sides.text: B. The route with the lowest administrative distance

more.text: AD ranks routing sources; metric ranks routes within one source.

sides.text: What is the default administrative distance of OSPF?

more.text: EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, RIP 120.

sides.text: Which command creates a default route to 203.0.113.1?

more.text: A default route is 0.0.0.0/0.

sides.text: A static route has AD 130. What is it?
A. A floating static route

more.text: Higher AD than the primary means it backs up.

sides.text: Which OSPF value breaks a DR election tie after priority?
B. Highest router ID

more.text: Priority first, then router ID.

sides.text: What is the OSPF cost of a 100 Mbps interface with the default reference bandwidth?
Which two values must match for OSPF neighbors to form?
D. Hello and dead timers

more.text: Timers, area, subnet, authentication, and MTU must match; router IDs must differ.

sides.text: What is the OSPF neighbor state of two DROTHER routers on a broadcast segment?
A. 2-Way

more.text: Only DR/BDR become Full with others.

sides.text: Which wildcard mask matches 10.1.4.0/22 in an OSPF network command?
Which command lists OSPF neighbors?
C. show ip ospf neighbor

more.text: Neighbor shows state and DR role.

sides.text: Which route code indicates a locally connected interface address?
D. L

more.text: L is the /32 local route; C is the connected network.

sides.text: What is the gateway of last resort?
options: The default route used when nothing more specific matches

sides.text: A. The default route used when nothing more specific matches

more.text: Shown at the top of the routing table.

sides.text: Which FHRP is Cisco proprietary and uses an active/standby model?
B. HSRP

more.text: VRRP is the open standard; GLBP is Cisco load balancing.

sides.text: What does a router do first when a packet arrives?
options: Matches the destination to the routing table by longest prefix

sides.text: C. Matches the destination to the routing table by longest prefix

more.text: Prefix specificity beats AD and metric.

sides.text: Which OSPF router connects an area to the backbone?
D. ABR

more.text: Area Border Router.

sides.text: Which command prevents OSPF hellos on an interface while still advertising its network?
A. passive-interface

more.text: Useful on user LAN interfaces.

sides.text: How is an OSPF router ID chosen when no router-id command exists?
options: Highest loopback IP, else highest active interface IP

sides.text: B. Highest loopback IP, else highest active interface IP

more.text: Manual configuration wins.

sides.text: An IPv6 static route to 2001:db8:2::/64 needs which prior command?
C. ipv6 unicast-routing

more.text: IPv6 routing is off by default.

sides.text: Which type of route is learned with the code S*?
D. A static default route

more.text: S static, * candidate default.

sides.text: Two equal-cost OSPF paths exist. What happens?
options: Traffic is load balanced across both

sides.text: A. Traffic is load balanced across both

more.text: ECMP up to 4 paths by default.

sides.text: A route shows [110/20]. What are the two numbers?
B. Administrative distance and metric

more.text: AD first, then metric.

sides.text: Which OSPF packet type establishes neighbor relationships?
C. Hello

more.text: Hellos discover and maintain neighbors.

sides.text: A neighbor is stuck in ExStart. Which issue is most likely?
D. MTU mismatch

more.text: Timer or area mismatches stop at Init/2-Way.

sides.text: Which protocol has a 15-hop maximum before routes are unreachable?
A. RIP

more.text: 16 hops is infinity in RIP.
